executiveSummary: U.S. election stakeholders face elevated risk from AI-generated impersonation, deepfake audio/video, and coordinated influence operations. The FBI and CISA issued a fresh advisory warning that adversaries are deploying deepfake media alongside phishing and smishing to target campaigns and election offices View Article . A companion FBI IC3 alert details active scams using AI-generated voices, images, and messages to impersonate candidates and trusted civic brands for fraudulent fundraising and identity theft View Article . Courts are escalating responses to synthetic-media risks. The federal judiciary formally added deepfakes to rulemaking discussions, including a proposal to address authenticity challenges, while industry warned that increasingly convincing fabrications outpace current detection Supporting Report View Article . Operational fraud remains severe: veterans were defrauded via deepfake phishing that diverted benefits View Article , and large-scale financial losses were reported in voice-clone and deepfake video-call schemes targeting enterprises and banking workflows View Article Supporting Report . The defensive landscape is mixed. Provenance tooling expanded (C2PA, SynthID), and platforms announced new scam-detection features View Article Supporting Report , but research shows deepfake detectors can dramatically fail against new models and adversarial perturbations View Article . Overall, the threat environment appears to be worsening as election-targeted activity intensifies and evidentiary trust is strained.
